summary:
[00:00:00–00:05:00] This video clip introduces a large-scale quantitative backtest of classical price action trading concepts using Claude to build and run test systems. Analyzing five years of one-minute data across NQ and ES futures representing over 327 million simulated trades across 101,345 system configurations, the presenter defines key price action mechanics (support/resistance levels, trend break of structure, change of character, sweeps, confirmation, stops, and targets), examines how subjective discretionary chart interpretations are formalized into objective testable rules, and highlights initial findings such as the strength of the change of character setup and the 50% reversal rate of liquidity sweeps.

[00:05:00–00:10:00] This clip evaluates price action trading concepts using backtests across 5 years of 1-minute NQ and ES futures data covering 327 million simulated trades across 101,345 rule variations. The analysis demonstrates that win rate does not track overall profitability (correlation 0.27), trading lower timeframes like the 1-minute chart is penalized heavily by costs (46% of gross profit), support and resistance levels demonstrably hold better than random lines (51.1% vs 42.4%), more touches do not make a level stronger, and flip zones provide significant positive predictive edge (+11.5 percentage points).

[00:10:00–00:15:00] This clip evaluates price action trading concepts using backtests on historical and unseen locked-forward futures data (NQ and ES). The author analyzes trend setups, trigger mechanisms, stop-loss types, context filters, and timeframe performance, finding that higher timeframes (4-hour and daily), 4-hour change-of-character (CHoCH) reversals without sweeps, hard stops, New York trading hours, and confirmation candles produce positive results, while close-based stops and daily trend alignment filters detract from edge.

[00:15:00–00:17:10] In this final segment, the presenter emphasizes that across extensive backtesting—including 9,000 algorithmic strategies, ICT sweep fades, and price action 4-hour change-of-character setups—mean reversion consistently emerges as the sole foundational principle that holds up. He then shares the five sequential prompts of his 'Price Action Lab' architecture, allowing viewers to build, automate, and rigorously backtest these systems in Python using LLMs like Claude Code or ChatGPT without look-ahead bias or overfitting.

segments.topic: Overview of the 100,000+ Price Action Concept Test
key_points: Tested over 100,000 price action concept variations using Claude to determine what actually works versus fancy indicators.
Ran 40,000 exploratory samples plus thousands of common configurations across nearly 5 years of 1-minute data on NQ and ES futures.
Simulated over 327 million trades to eliminate reliance on anecdotal single-trader claims.
Presenter background: studied Math and Econ at UCLA, worked in investment banking at Raymond James for 3+ years, and spent 2 years building trading systems.

segments.topic: Core Price Action Concepts and Preliminary Findings
key_points: Price action is defined as trading directly off the chart itself without secondary indicators.
Levels (support and resistance) beat random lines on timeframes from 5-minute to daily.
Trend is defined as series of higher highs and higher lows; a break of structure occurs when price closes above the last high.
Trend continuation showed no statistically meaningful follow-through on any chart timeframe tested.
Change of Character (CHoCH) occurs when price breaks and closes below the last higher low; this held up as the best-performing setup, especially on the 4-hour timeframe.

Sweeps (wicking past a key high or low where stop-losses sit and closing back inside) reversed only about half the time (~50%), meaning it functions as a secondary signal rather than a standalone edge.
Confirmation (e.g., waiting for a candle close rather than entering with a limit order at the level) beat limit entries on NQ.
Hard stops beat close-based stops; on the profit-target side, there was no measurable edge across variations.
Higher timeframes consistently yielded more profitable strategy variations.

segments.topic: The Ten Price Action Setups Tested
key_points: Identified 10 primary setups: Level bounce, Breakout, Flip zone, Trend pullback, Trend line, Break of structure, Change of character, Sweep and reclaim, Supply and demand, and Fair value gap.
Promotion of the presenter's AI trading community on Skool covering stocks, options, crypto, and futures, and 1-on-1 trading system development.

segments.topic: Testing Methodology: Overcoming 'Drawn By Eye' Discretion
key_points: Traditional price action trading suffers from subjectivity ('drawn by eye') where different traders draw different levels on the exact same chart.
Algorithmic rules applied to define discretionary elements: Level requires 2+ swings within 0.25 ATR; Touch defined as within 0.25 ATR of the level; Confirmation defined as a close back across it.
Parameter space spans 20.3 trillion theoretical combinations across specific 'dials': touches, line vs. zone, confirmation, stop logic, target logic, chart timeframe, and filters.
Tested 40,000 dial spreads (4,000 per setup) plus 61,345 common configurations (0 to 2 filters) totaling 101,345 tested model versions.

Evaluation gauntlet includes real transaction costs, slippage on every stop, treating ambiguous candles as losses, benchmarking against random lines and random trades, cross-checking on ES, and a 2-year locked-away out-of-sample dataset.

segments.topic: Backtest Setup and Testing Scale
key_points: Parameter space contains 20.3 trillion possible versions across different dials (touches, line/zone, confirmation, stop, target, chart, filters).
Ran 40,000 randomized versions (4,000 per setup across 10 setups) plus 61,345 common versions (usual settings, 0 to 2 filters), totaling 101,345 tested strategy versions.
Data consists of 5 years of 1-minute bars on NQ and ES futures (3.6 million bars, 327 million simulated trades).

Backtesting system built in Python via Claude with 'The Gauntlet': real costs, slippage on every trade/step, ambiguous bars treated as losses, comparisons against random lines and random trades, and a 2-year out-of-sample lock on ES.

segments.topic: Discovery Funnel Results
key_points: Out of 101,345 tested versions, 88,986 generated enough trades (30+) to be graded.
24,879 of 101,345 versions (~24.5%) made money after trading costs in NQ discovery.
8,310 versions (~8.2%) cleared a Sharpe ratio threshold of 0.5+.

segments.topic: Win Rate vs Profit Analysis
key_points: Claims of 80%+ win rates in price action trading are largely unfounded; only 138 of 40,000 strategies reached an 80%+ win rate.
67 of the 138 strategies achieving an 80%+ win rate relied on a 1R profit target.
Across all 40,000 strategies, win rate showed weak correlation with profit (correlation coefficient of 0.27).

segments.topic: Timeframe Performance and Cost Friction
key_points: Costs eat up 46.0% of gross profit on the 1-minute timeframe versus only 3.9% on the Daily timeframe.
Percentage of profitable versions increases from 32% on 1-minute to 47% on Daily.
Median annual PnL per contract is -$428k on 1m, -$308k on 5m, -$210k on 15m, -$4k on 1h, +$3k on 4h, and +$6k on Daily.
Trading higher timeframes (1h, 4h, Daily) requires less trading edge because overhead costs and slippage represent a much smaller percentage of gross gains.

segments.topic: Support & Resistance Validity and Touch Count Myth
key_points: Real horizontal support/resistance levels held 51.1% of touches across 5m to Daily charts compared to 42.4% for random lines (+8.7 points outperformance on NQ, +8.5 points on ES).
Testing the myth that 'more touches equal stronger levels': 1 touch beat random lines by +9.0 points, 2 touches by +7.8 points, 3 touches by +8.2 points, and 4 touches by +6.1 points.
Levels touched 3+ times bounced less frequently (19.2% vs 20.5%) and broke through more often (27.8% vs 26.1%) compared to 1 touch.

segments.topic: Level Rules and Flip Zones Edge
key_points: Testing various level rules: Touch count showed -1.1 pts effect; Wall at 3+ touches showed -1.3 pts; Weaker pushes showed +0.4 pts; Box vs line showed +0.5 pts.
Flip zones (prior resistance becoming support or vice versa) outperformed random baselines by +11.5 percentage points on NQ and +10.9 percentage points on ES.

segments.topic: Level Rules and Flip Zones
key_points: Flip zones outperformed other level rules, adding +11.5 percentage points overall and +10.9 points on ES.
Touch count (-1.1 pts) and wall at 3+ touches (-1.3 pts) reduced performance.
The speaker concludes flip zones are the strongest and most important concept in price action besides basic support and resistance.

segments.topic: Trend Setups: BOS vs CHoCH and Sweeps
key_points: Break of structure (-0.04 ATR) and change of character (-0.05 ATR) do not predict price follow-through on their own.
Among trend setups, only change of character (CHoCH) reversal had a positive median profit (+$61), while BOS continuation (-$328), sweep and reclaim (-$368), and trend line (-$479) were negative.
Testing the conventional rule of waiting for a sweep before a change of character lost -$834 on unseen locked data, whereas taking the CHoCH without a sweep made +$903.

segments.topic: Trigger: Confirmation Tax vs Limit Orders
key_points: Waiting for a candle confirmation gives up 4.3 points of price entry relative to a limit order at the touch.
Despite worse execution price, waiting for confirmation increased edge by +$719 per year on Nasdaq futures (-$373 loss vs -$1,093 loss for limit at touch).

segments.topic: Exit Types: Hard Stop vs Close-Based Stop
key_points: Close-based stops (exiting only when a candle closes beyond the level) win more frequently (40% vs 29%), but result in larger losses.
Overall, close-based stops cost $132 more per year (-$290 vs -$158 for hard stops), meaning a plain hard stop performs better.

segments.topic: Context Filters: Trading Hours, Run Skips, and Daily Trend
key_points: Trading only during New York session hours (8:00 AM to 4:00 PM ET) improved performance by +$270 per year on unseen NQ.
Skipping trades after 3+ day directional runs improved performance by +$246.
Filtering trades to align with the daily trend hurt performance significantly (-$587).

segments.topic: Consistency Check: Setups Passing Both NQ and ES
key_points: Across 40,000 tested variants and common versions, only the 4-hour change of character (CHoCH) passed in both NQ and ES markets across all sets.
On NQ, 4h CHoCH returned +$4,025/year (original) and +$4,884/year (common versions). On ES, it returned +$4,146/year (original) and +$3,374/year (common versions).

segments.topic: Timeframe Ladder in Final Locked Window
key_points: The final test window (2025-2026) experienced a 22.5% selloff and a 74.5% rally.
Strategy profitability correlates directly with higher timeframes: 1m made money on 9.2% of versions, 5m on 20.3%, 15m on 28.8%, 1h on 37.7%, 4h on 45.1%, and Daily on 47.9%.
On NQ specifically, 45% of 4h versions made money versus only 9% of 1m versions.

segments.topic: Best 4h Setup Performance on Locked Data
key_points: The best version (4h CHoCH, no sweep, candle close entry, hard stop past last swing, 1:1 risk-to-reward) earned +$62,179 on 1 NQ contract and +$39,284 on ES over 2 locked years.
NQ locked-period stats: 61 trades, 54% win rate.
Robustness test: 39 of 48 usual setting versions (81%) and 66% of 314 common versions made money on NQ; 54.5% made money on ES.
Average New York session version made +$17,041 per contract and remained profitable even excluding the 10 best days.

segments.topic: Summary of Surviving Price Action Principles and Example Trade
key_points: Seven rules survived: (1) 4h CHoCH, (2) higher timeframe charts, (3) New York session only, (4) skip trades into 3+ day runs, (5) confirmation candle on NQ, (6) hard stop instead of close-based, (7) no sweep required before the change.
Walkthrough of an example trade on NQ 4h from July 11, 2024 showing entry at close, swing-high stop, and 1:1 target.
Comparison with previous channel studies: 9,000 strategies (mean reversion), ICT (fading the sweep), and price action (4h CHoCH).

segments.topic: What Kept Working: Mean Reversion as the Baseline
key_points: In the 9,000 strategies test, mean reversion was the only strategy type that held up across thousands of variations.
In the ICT test, the only version that held up was fading the sweep, which is fundamentally a mean-reversion strategy.
The 4-hour change-of-character setup is a reversal setup that also operates as a mean-reversion strategy.
The core concept is that when price stretches too high or too low, it reverts.
These test results represent 'the floor, not the ceiling'—a foundational baseline averaged across one contract per trade, meant to have risk management and position sizing layered on top.

segments.topic: Build It Yourself: The Five Prompts Framework
key_points: Viewers can replicate the entire testing framework by running five sequential prompts in Claude Code or ChatGPT.

Prompt 1 (Data and dials): sets up Python venv, data ingestion (NQ/ES 1-minute continuous front-month data, sha256 hashing), cleaning, warm-up (2021-10-01 to 2021-12-31), discovery (2022-01-03 to 2024-07-31), and sealed out-of-sample window (from 2024-08-01 onward), plus multi-timeframe bar creation and dial specifications (over 20 trillion combinations).

Prompt 2 (Engine and level tests): builds the single-contract trade engine with explicit costs ($4 commission per round trip, 1 tick slippage on market/stops), checks (including 20,000 random entries losing ~$9.80/trade), and behavior tests on levels and patterns against random baselines.

Prompt 3 (The funnel): tests 40,000 random configurations, 14,016 grid versions, and 47,320 trader-style samples across a 5-step filter (trade count >= 30, win rate > 50%, Sharpe >= 0.5, beat 10,000 twin random trades at p < 0.05, hold on ES with Sharpe >= 0.3).
Prompt 4 (The final test): unseals the held-out test data once with an access log guard, verifying hashed configurations and evaluating final candidates without modifying any dials.
Prompt 5 (The dashboard): generates a 1920x1080 static HTML presentation dashboard with full data provenance checks where every on-screen number traces to a saved file.

segments.topic: Conclusion and Outro
key_points: The presenter emphasizes that any trading style based on intuition can be codified into rules and tested at scale with real data.
Channel outro call to action (like, comment, subscribe, community link, and 1-on-1 booking link).

claims.claim: Trend continuation (break of structure) shows no statistically valid follow-through on any chart timeframe.
Change of character (CHoCH) held up the best out of all tested price action concepts, performing best on the 4-hour chart.
claims.caveats: Specific Sharpe ratio, win rate, and return numbers are not detailed in this introductory segment.

claims.claim: Liquidity sweeps reverse only about half the time (~50%) and lack standalone edge without additional confluence.
claims.caveats: Can be helpful as a confluence signal but not as an independent core entry system.

claims.claim: Support and resistance levels beat random lines across timeframes from the 5-minute to daily charts.
Price action strategies rarely achieve 80%+ win rates, and win rate is poorly correlated with total profit.
claims.caveats: 67 of the 138 high win-rate strategies used 1R targets, which skew win rate at the expense of payoff ratio.

claims.claim: Friction from trading costs and slippage severely impairs 1-minute strategies compared to higher timeframes.
claims.caveats: Assumes standard futures commissions and slippage on every trade step.

claims.claim: Support and resistance levels have genuine statistical validity over random lines.
claims.caveats: Tested across timeframes from 5-minute to Daily on NQ and ES futures.

claims.claim: Repeated touches do not make a support or resistance level stronger; levels with 4 touches hold less frequently than levels with 1 touch.
claims.caveats: Specific individual setups may succeed, but the aggregate tendency over 300M+ trades shows diminished holding rates with additional touches.

claims.claim: Flip zones hold significantly better on first retest than ordinary support and resistance levels.
claims.caveats: Evaluated on first retest after a breakout.

claims.claim: Flip zones are the strongest and most effective price action level concept.
Break of structure and change of character on their own do not move price or predict price direction.
Requiring a liquidity sweep before a change of character setup loses money in out-of-sample data.
claims.caveats: Tested over two locked out-of-sample years on index futures.

claims.claim: Waiting for a confirmation candle rather than entering at the touch with a limit order improves net performance despite giving up 4.3 points of price.
Close-based stops achieve a higher win rate (40% vs 29%) but result in larger losses and poorer overall performance than hard stops.
Filtering trades to align with the daily trend significantly hurts price action setup performance.
Price action strategies have a substantially higher likelihood of being profitable on higher timeframes (4h, Daily) than on 1m or 5m charts.
Mean reversion was the only strategy style that held up across 9,000 strategy variations, ICT sweep fading, and price action change-of-character tests.
claims.caveats: Performance figures represent the baseline 'floor' averaged across all unoptimized versions with 1 contract per trade, before adding sizing or risk management.

claims.claim: A random entry baseline of 20,000 trades with a 1R ATR stop and 2R target loses approximately -$9.80 per trade after costs.
claims.caveats: Measured on discovery data with $4 commission and 1 tick slippage applied.

visuals.title: The Ten Setups

2. Breakout - trade the close through a level
3. Flip zone - old resistance becomes support
4. Trend pullback - buy the first dip in an uptrend
5. Trend line - buy a touch of the rising line
6. Break of structure - go with the break of the last swing
7. Change of character - the first break against the trend
8. Sweep and reclaim - a wick through a low, closed back above
9. Supply and demand - the first return to an impulse's base
10. Fair value gap - the first return into a three-candle gap

visuals.title: PROMPT 1 OF 5 / Data and dials
values_readable: WHAT THIS BUILDS: A Python research lab that turns price action trading rules into exact rules a computer can test on NQ and ES futures...

RULES: Work in one project folder with a Python virtual environment. Save every result as a file, and log each decision and its reason in decisions.md. Fix a master seed... The final window stays sealed... Never move a threshold after seeing a result...
INPUTS: 1-minute NQ and ES continuous front-month futures... Copy each unchanged into data/raw/ and record its sha256... ts_event, open, high, low, close, volume, contract...
visuals.what_it_argues: Specifies environment setup, data ingestion rules, and cryptographic hashing for Prompt 1.

visuals.title: PROMPT 1 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: CLEAN AND CHECK: Convert to America/New_York. Session 18:00 to 17:00 ET dated by end day. Audit duplicates, inverted high/low, missing minutes, 17:00 halt hour drop. Back-adjusted bars for signals/fills. No entries 60m before roll. News calendar of CPI, Jobs report, FOMC.

WINDOWS: Warm-up: 2021-10-01 to 2021-12-31; Discovery: 2022-01-03 to 2024-07-31 (Era 1: 2022, Era 2: 2023 to July 2024); Final: 2024-08-01 to latest (data 2026-10-16 here) sealed with sha256 manifest and file reader guard.

visuals.title: PROMPT 1 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: CHARTS: Build 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h and daily bars from 1-minute bars from 18:00 open. 4h bars: 18-22, 22-02, 02-06, 06-10, 10-14, 14-17 ET. Higher timeframe bar usable only from its close. ATR is Wilder's 14-bar ATR.

THE DIALS: Ten setups: level bounce, breakout, flip zone, trend pullback, trend line, break of structure continuation, change of character reversal, sweep and reclaim, supply and demand zone, fair value gap.

Six setup charts (5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, daily) with trigger charts. Swing strength 2, 3, 5, 8. Level clusters within 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 ATR (1-4 touches). Supply/demand zones 2-5 candles covering 1.5-3 ATR. Three-candle FVG.

visuals.what_it_argues: Details shared execution dials and filters, showing the theoretical search space spans 20.26 trillion valid versions.

visuals.title: PROMPT 2 OF 5 / Engine and level tests
values_readable: WHAT THIS BUILDS: Trade engine and behavior tests asking whether price respects levels, flips, breaks, sweeps, gaps, zones more than chance.
INPUTS: Cleaned 1m bars of NQ and ES in discovery window, derived MTF bars with ATR, roll times, news days, detectors.
RULES: Master seed, no look-ahead bias (unit test: mock detector run on cut data must equal full run).
visuals.what_it_argues: Sets requirements for the backtesting engine and anti-lookahead unit tests.

visuals.title: PROMPT 2 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: THE ENGINE: 1 contract per trade (half-size on news, 1 position at a time per strategy). No overnight hold unless flat at 16:00. Every fill/exit checked on 1m bars.
Costs: $4 commission round trip, 1 tick slippage on market entries, hard stops, close stops, structure exits. No slippage on limits, targets, time exits, roll exits.
Limit fills only when 1m bar trades 1 tick through. Hard stop exits 1 tick worse than stop or open. Ambiguous candle (stop and target hit in same 1m bar) counts as loss.
Tick sizes: NQ: $20/point; ES: 0.25 tick, $50/point. Sharpe is mean over standard deviation of daily P&L times sqrt(252).
visuals.what_it_argues: Defines explicit fill logic, execution constraints, transaction costs, and tick math for realistic backtesting.

visuals.title: PROMPT 2 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: ENGINE CHECKS: Unit tests on made-up price paths; 20,000 market entries at random discovery minutes with 1R ATR stop and 2R target lose -$9.80/trade after costs; intentional look-ahead cheat test makes money.
BEHAVIOR TESTS: Measure price action after events vs random stand-in on NQ and ES (5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, daily). Swing strength 3, 0.25 ATR tolerance.
Random lines: move real levels up/down 1 to 3 ATR (>=0.5 ATR from real level); random remedies with 20 random bars.
visuals.what_it_argues: Establishes sanity-check benchmarks and behavior statistical tests against randomized levels.

visuals.title: PROMPT 2 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: THE TESTS: real levels against random lines; hold rate by touch count; shrinking bounces; wick vs close through level; flip zones; follow-through at 10, 20, 50 bars; sweeps; trend lines; FVG; supply/demand zones; pullback depth; rejection candles.
Intervals: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of whole sessions, 95% intervals.
Verdict: true when NQ interval excludes zero, ES agrees in sign, and both eras agree; split when partly holds; false otherwise.
visuals.what_it_argues: Defines statistical bootstrapping and multi-era criteria to evaluate whether price action concepts have an edge.

visuals.title: PROMPT 3 OF 5 / The funnel
values_readable: WHAT THIS BUILDS: Funnel filtering hundreds of thousands of strategy versions.
THE VERSIONS: Random set of 40,000 versions (4,000 per setup), requiring >=40 signals on NQ discovery.
visuals.what_it_argues: Outlines candidate generation across the search space.

visuals.title: PROMPT 3 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: Six named versions: Bare Minimum, Daily Version, Checklist, Sweep System, Trend System, Ultra-Safe.
Trader sample: 47,320 versions (40% no filter, 40% 1 filter, 20% 2 filters).
THE FUNNEL: 1. Trades >= 30; 2. Win rate > 50%; 3. Sharpe >= 0.5.
visuals.what_it_argues: Defines the test batches and initial filter thresholds.

visuals.title: PROMPT 3 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: 4. Beat matched random trades: 10,000 sets of twin random trades; pass when <5% of sets match performance.
5. Hold on ES: profitable on ES discovery with Sharpe >= 0.3.
Final-test candidate: passes 1 to 4, profitable in both eras (2022 and 2023-2024), holds on ES.
JUDGE SETUP: Average daily P&L across all versions with equal weight; profitable per year, Sharpe >= 0.5, profitable in 2022 and 2023-24.
visuals.what_it_argues: Defines advanced filter steps (Monte Carlo twin test and cross-asset validation on ES) to eliminate curve-fitting.

visuals.title: PROMPT 4 OF 5 / The final test
values_readable: WHAT THIS BUILDS: Final test on sealed data (NQ and ES 1m bars from 2024-08-01).
RULES: No dial or threshold changes. Check sha256 hashes. Rehearse on shifted last month of discovery. Single logged unlock.
visuals.what_it_argues: Specifies strict out-of-sample testing protocols preventing data snooping.

visuals.title: PROMPT 4 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: THE RUN: Warm up detectors from 2024-05-01. Score on NQ and ES over final window with identical costs and fill logic.
WHAT HELD UP: Version held up if profitable after costs with Sharpe >= 0.5. Setup held up if equal-weight average made money per year with Sharpe >= 0.5.
visuals.what_it_argues: Specifies execution and success criteria on the held-out final test period.

visuals.title: PROMPT 5 OF 5 / The dashboard
values_readable: WHAT THIS BUILDS: Presentation dashboard with full provenance tracking.
RULES: Every number on screen must trace to a saved file. Provenance file records source file, row, column, format, and displayed text. Double read verification. Facecam cutout 520x368 px.
PAGE: Offline static HTML, 1920x1080 stage, navy background (#0b0f1a), cyan and amber accents.
visuals.what_it_argues: Details UI dashboard generation and data integrity verification for results presentation.

visuals.title: PROMPT 5 OF 5 · CONTINUED
values_readable: Each finding gets a page: eyebrow section, title, one-line subtitle, 1 chart, max 2 big stats, conclusion badge ('survived, split or didn't survive').
Checks in headless Chrome at 1920x1080 and 1280x720. Provenance check must pass on every number.
visuals.what_it_argues: Specifies automated QA testing for visual presentation slides.

strategies.name: Change of Character (CHoCH)
strategies.logic: Identifies the first structural break against an established trend (e.g. price closing below the prior higher low in an uptrend) to enter in the direction of the trend reversal.
entry_rules: In an uptrend, wait for price to close below the most recent higher low swing level.
Enter on candle confirmation closing past the level.
exit_rules: Hard stop-loss placed beyond the swing high.
strategies.stated_performance: Identified as holding up the best out of all price action findings.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: Backtested with real costs on every trade and slippage on every stop.

strategies.name: Algorithmic Level Support/Resistance Bounce
strategies.logic: Identifies horizontal support/resistance levels mathematically using ATR cluster rules and trades the bounce upon confirmation.
entry_rules: Identify level where 2 or more swings occur within 0.25 ATR of each other.
Price touches within 0.25 ATR of the level.
Confirmation candle closes back across the level.
exit_rules: Hard stop-loss beat close-based stop; profit targets showed no edge.
strategies.stated_performance: Beat random lines from 5m to daily timeframes; confirmation entry beat limit orders on NQ.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: Tested against gauntlet with real costs, slippage on every stop, and ambiguous candles counted as losses.

strategies.name: Price Action Support/Resistance & Flip Zones
strategies.logic: Trading bounces or breakouts from identified horizontal support/resistance levels and flip zones (broken resistance becoming support or vice versa).
entry_rules: Price touches a defined support/resistance level or flip zone.
Optional confirmation candle or filter as parameterized.
exit_rules: Stop-loss placed past the level or last swing.
Target exit based on fixed R-multiple (e.g. 1R, 1.5R, 2R, 3R, 4R, 5R) or next structure level.
strategies.stated_performance: 24,879 of 101,345 versions were profitable after costs; flip zones hold +11.5 pts over random on NQ and +10.9 pts on ES.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: Full trading commissions deducted on every trade, slippage applied on every execution step, ambiguous intraday bars counted as full losses.

strategies.name: 4-Hour Change of Character Reversal (Best Version)
strategies.logic: Enter a mean reversion/reversal trade following a Change of Character (CHoCH) on a 4-hour chart without requiring a preceding liquidity sweep.
entry_rules: Identify an established trend on the 4-hour chart.
Wait for a Change of Character (first candle close in the opposite direction breaking market structure).
Enter at the close of the confirming 4-hour candle (optionally restricted to New York session: 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET; avoid trading in the direction of an extended 3+ day run).
exit_rules: Place a hard stop immediately beyond the last swing extreme (e.g., swing high for a short setup). Do not use a close-based stop.
Set profit target at 1:1 risk-to-reward (target size equals risk size).

parameters.name: Session Filter
parameters.value: New York session only (8:00 AM to 4:00 PM ET)

parameters.name: Trend Run Filter
parameters.value: Skip trades into a 3+ day run

strategies.stated_performance: +$62,179 on NQ (61 trades, 54% win rate) and +$39,284 on ES over 2 locked years per contract.

strategies.name: 4h Change of Character Reversal (Mean Reversion)
strategies.logic: Reversal mean-reversion setup where price stretches excessively on the 4-hour chart and triggers an entry upon a change of character (first close past the last swing high/low).
entry_rules: Price stretches too high or too low.
Change of character confirmed by the first close past the last swing on the 4-hour chart (or lower trigger chart).
exit_rules: Take profit targets set at 1R, 1.5R, 2R, 3R, 5R, 10R or next swing.
Stop loss set beyond the level or swing point with 0 to 0.25 ATR buffer.
Time exit at 16:00, 16:40, or after 24/96 bars.
strategies.stated_performance: Serves as an average baseline ('floor') that held up across thousands of tested iterations.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: $4 commission per round trip, 1 tick slippage on market entries and stop exits.
